body.title: bug: No Query Timeout - Long-running queries can hang indefinitely with no cancellation mechanism
body.body: ### Summary NexumDB does not enforce query execution timeouts, allowing long-running or inefficient queries to run indefinitely with no cancellation mechanism. This can cause the database to appear hung, consume CPU/memory resources indefinitely, and block other queries, especially in production or shared environments. ### Steps to Reproduce Start a NexumDB instance. Execute a long-running or unoptimized query, for example: SELECT * FROM users CROSS JOIN large_table; or any query that scans a large dataset without indexes. It lacks command history (up arrow) and syntax highlighting. ## Requirements - Replace basic input with a crate like `rustyline` or `reedline`. - Implement persistence for command history (~/.nexum_history). - (Optional) Add basic SQL syntax highlighting. ## Impact - Significantly improves developer experience and usability.

body.title: feat: Add DROP TABLE support
body.body: ## Description The SQL parser misses support for `DROP TABLE` statements. ## Requirements - Update `sql/parser.rs` to support `DROP TABLE table_name`. - Update `sql/planner.rs` and executor to handle table deletion. - Ensure metadata is removed from catalog and data is wiped from storage. ## Impact - Allows users to manage schema lifecycle properly.

body.title: feat: Add UPDATE statement support
body.body: ## Description The SQL parser currently misses support for `UPDATE` statements. ## Requirements - Update `sql/parser.rs` to support `UPDATE table SET col = val WHERE ...`. - Update `sql/planner.rs` to create an update plan. - Implement update logic in `executor/mod.rs`. ## Impact - Required for full CRUD functionality.

body.title: feat: Add EXPLAIN query plan command
body.body: ## Description Users have no visibility into how their queries are being executed or optimized by the AI engine. ## Requirements - Implement an `EXPLAIN <query>` command. - Output should show: - The parsed SQL structure. - Whether the result was served from cache (and the cache similarity score). - The execution path chosen by the RL agent (with Q-values if possible). ## Impact - Critical for debugging and understanding AI optimization decisions.

body.title: feat: Add DELETE statement support
body.body: ## Summary Currently, the SQL parser in `nexum_core/src/sql/parser.rs` supports `CREATE TABLE`, `INSERT`, and `SELECT`. Support for `DELETE` statements is missing. ## Scope - Update `parser.rs` to handle `DELETE FROM table [WHERE condition]`. - Update `planner.rs` to create a deletion plan. - Implement deletion logic in `executor/mod.rs` and storage engine. ## Impact - Essential for full CRUD capability.

body.title: feat: Implement persistence for RL Agent Q-Table
body.body: ## Description The Reinforcement Learning agent in `nexum_ai/optimizer.py` learns optimal query execution strategies, but the Q-table is currently stored only in memory. ## Requirements - Implement methods to save and load the Q-table (e.g., using pickle or json). - Ensure the agent loads previous learning state on startup. - Configure a persistent path for the model file. ## Impact - Enables the database to get smarter over time, even across restarts. - Fulfills the 'Persistent Learning' feature promise significantly.

body.title: feat: Implement semantic cache persistence to disk
body.body: ## Description The current semantic cache implementation in `nexum_ai/optimizer.py` is purely in-memory. This means all cached query embeddings and results are lost when the database service restarts. ## Requirements - Implement disk-based persistence for the semantic cache (e.g., using pickle, json, or a lightweight DB like SQLite/DuckDB). - Ensure cache is loaded on startup. - Add cache eviction policy (LRU or similar) to prevent unbounded growth. ## Impact - Significantly improves cold-start performance after restarts. - Allows the AI engine to retain learned query similarities over time.

body.title: Implement cost-based query optimizer
body.body: Add a query optimizer with cost-based planning: 1. Collect table statistics (row count, column cardinality, histograms) 2. Implement cost model for different operations 3. Generate multiple query plans and choose lowest cost 4. Optimize join order for multi-table queries 5. Add `EXPLAIN` command to show query plans This significantly improves query performance on larger datasets.

body.title: Implement structured error types with thiserror
body.body: Implement a proper error handling strategy across the codebase: 1. Define custom error types using `thiserror` in each module 2. Implement `From` conversions for error propagation 3. Replace `anyhow` with typed errors in library code (keep `anyhow` in CLI) 4. Add error codes for programmatic error handling 5. Ensure all errors have useful context messages This improves debuggability and allows callers to handle specific error cases.

body.title: Implement transaction support (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK)
body.body: Add transaction support with ACID guarantees: 1. Implement `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK` commands 2. Add write-ahead logging (WAL) for durability 3. Implement MVCC for isolation (or simpler locking initially) 4. Add transaction ID tracking 5. Handle crash recovery from WAL This is foundational for a production-ready database.

body.title: Implement TCP server with wire protocol
body.body: Implement a connection pooling and client protocol: 1. Define wire protocol (consider PostgreSQL wire protocol subset for compatibility) 2. Implement TCP server in `nexum_cli` or new `nexum_server` crate 3. Add connection handling with async (tokio) 4. Implement connection pooling for concurrent clients 5. Add authentication (simple password or certificate-based) 6. Create client library or document compatible clients This enables NexumDB to be used as a networked database server.

Add corpus of valid and invalid SQL statements 4. Configure CI to run fuzzing periodically (or on schedule) 5. Document how to run fuzzing locally This helps catch parsing bugs and potential security issues with malformed input.

Add tests for `optimizer.py` (query optimization logic) 4. Add tests for `rl_agent.py` (RL training loop, state/action handling) 5. Add tests for `translator.py` (NL to SQL translation) 6. Add mocks for expensive operations (model loading, GPU) 7. Add pytest to CI workflow Target: >80% coverage for nexum_ai.

body.title: Implement JOIN support in SQL executor
body.body: Add support for `JOIN` operations in the SQL executor: 1. Parse `INNER JOIN`, `LEFT JOIN`, `RIGHT JOIN` syntax 2. Extend query planner to create join nodes 3. Implement nested-loop join algorithm in executor 4. Add hash join for equi-joins (performance optimization) 5. Add integration tests for join queries Example queries to support: ```sql SELECT u.name, o.total FROM users u INNER JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id; SELECT * FROM products p LEFT JOIN inventory i ON p.id = i.product_id; ```

body.title: Implement aggregate functions and GROUP BY
body.body: Add aggregate functions and GROUP BY support: 1. Parse `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX` functions 2. Parse `GROUP BY` and `HAVING` clauses 3. Implement aggregation in executor with hash-based grouping 4. Handle `NULL` values correctly in aggregates 5. Add tests for edge cases (empty groups, all NULLs) ```sql SELECT department, COUNT(*), AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 5; ```

body.title: Add Dockerfile and docker-compose
body.body: Add Docker support for easy deployment and development: 1. Create `Dockerfile` for production builds (multi-stage, minimal image) 2. Create `docker-compose.yml` for local development 3. Add volume mounts for data persistence 4. Document Docker usage in README 5. Add CI job to build and push Docker image on release ```dockerfile FROM rust:1.75 AS builder WORKDIR /app COPY . . RUN cargo build --release FROM debian:bookworm-slim COPY --from=builder /app/target/release/nexum /usr/local/bin/ CMD ["nexum"] ```

body.title: Implement secondary index support
body.body: Add secondary index support for faster lookups: 1. Extend `CREATE INDEX` syntax in parser 2. Implement B-tree index structure in storage layer 3. Update query planner to use indexes when beneficial 4. Add index maintenance on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE 5. Support composite indexes ```sql CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email); CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_date ON orders(user_id, created_at); ```
